# Visual references and interpretation

This note records observations for Fluxo's UI-design skill. References are directional; do not reproduce the original artwork, text, brand identity, or exact layout.

## Twain — Awwwards

URL: https://www.awwwards.com/sites/twain

The public Awwwards description presents Twain as an AI go-to-market product that guides a prospect-research-to-outreach journey with a paper-plane metaphor, WebGL, and scroll choreography. The page itself was not available in the integrated browser during this review, so this is a verified description, not a claim that the live animation was inspected.

**Useful translation for Fluxo:** explain a complicated handoff as one journey. Use a small, authored narrative cue on sign-in, onboarding, or workflow introductions; show the current step and destination. Keep the ERP's daily operations static, fast, and easy to scan. Do not add WebGL, a paper-plane motif, or scrolling effects just because they appear in the reference description.

## AI Assistant Dashboard — Dribbble

URL: https://dribbble.com/shots/26081670-Dashboard-UI-Design-AI-Assistant

The linked page title identifies an AI-assistant dashboard UI. Dribbble blocked visual retrieval in this environment, so no palette, component placement, typography, or image details could be verified.

**Useful translation for Fluxo:** if a future assistant feature is approved, make it contextual to the selected demand and expose suggested actions with clear provenance and human confirmation. The reference does not authorize creating an assistant or fabricating its capabilities.

## CRM Dashboard App — Dribbble

URL: https://dribbble.com/shots/25742359-CRM-Dashboard-App-Design

The linked title identifies a CRM dashboard app design. Dribbble blocked visual retrieval in this environment, so this note does not infer a particular color scheme or composition.

**Useful translation for Fluxo:** prioritize familiar business-dashboard affordances: stable navigation, clear page title and filters, scannable records, explicit workflow status, and a visible next action. Use these as product principles, not as a copied screen.

## User-supplied reference screenshots

The user later supplied four screenshots, providing visual evidence beyond the original inaccessible Dribbble pages:

- The CRM board uses a white left navigation, a warm near-white/olive summary band, restrained black typography, compact metrics, and horizontally grouped cards by pipeline stage. Cards are white with fine neutral borders and small amounts of metadata.
- A second image shows the same CRM direction with General Sans and a palette of near-black, warm ivory, light gray, and white. Treat these as approximate visual cues, not required exact tokens or assets.
- The assistant dashboard uses a bright white workspace within a pale cool-lavender frame, a compact vertical icon rail, and three task cards. Translate only the spacious hierarchy and quiet lavender accent; do not add an assistant feature.
- The CRM workspace screenshot uses a light gray canvas, white document/activity panels, subtle periwinkle-blue controls, and a clear main-content/sidebar split. Avoid the exact branding, avatars, copy, and decorative composition.

These supplied screenshots were directly visible. This does not change the earlier limitation that the live Dribbble pages themselves could not be inspected.

The user later supplied a separate login-screen reference: a white account form on the left, a soft gray rounded narrative panel on the right, and restrained header/footer controls. Fluxo adapts this split composition with its own brand and a factual three-area workflow panel; it intentionally omits the reference's social sign-in choices, testimonial, and unrelated account controls.

The user also supplied a settings-menu reference with an icon rail and a larger account-navigation panel, plus a profile-card reference and a financial-analytics dashboard. Use the menu's focused active state and icon hierarchy only where the product has matching, authorized destinations; do not add fake settings. The profile-card image inspires a clearer account identity card, not invented ratings, earnings, skills, or contact actions. The analytics image inspires a light financial dashboard with a large chart, KPI stack, and supporting panels. Since Fluxo has no monthly financial series or expense ledger, use actual demand counts by workflow stage, total budgets, and recorded invoiced values instead of copying monthly income/expense charts or trends.

The menu reference's task-search field is adapted to filter only destinations available to the signed-in role, including the account profile. Preserve a clear no-results state and a one-click reset; do not make hidden/unauthorized destinations discoverable through search.

## Combined direction

Fluxo should feel like a professional CRM/ERP workspace: light navigation, warm neutral surfaces, ink-like text, restrained periwinkle interactive accents, and stage-based demand cards. Use compact real-data summaries and keep the integrated Commercial → Finance → People handoff more prominent than decoration. The entry screen uses a light split login and factual workflow introduction. Never claim visual review of a reference that could not be opened.

## UI UX Pro Max methodology reference

Source: https://github.com/nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill

This project skill uses the source's high-level workflow: identify the product and stack, establish a coherent design direction before coding, prioritize accessibility and interaction before polish, and verify responsive and stack-specific behavior. It is an original, project-specific workflow; it does not copy or vendor the upstream skill's datasets, scripts, or prose.
